html:
SMTO-HTTP-0034 — SMTO only got part of the service's reply

GUID: 2a911fb8-03ec-4495-94ec-49c6cb214978
Slug: http-response-incomplete
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service's answer stopped partway through or took too long to finish, so SMTO can't trust what arrived. The service may still have carried out the request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: look on the service, for example its website, for the record or change the task asked for. The service received the request; only its reply was cut off, so the change may be done.
  2. If the task only read information, run it again, asking for a smaller amount of data if the reply was large. Reading again changes nothing, and a smaller reply finishes before the time limit.
  3. If a change did not happen, make sure the Gateway's computer has a steady network connection, then run the task again. An unstable connection is a common reason a reply is cut off partway.

What success looks like

  • A repeated read returns the full answer, and you've confirmed any earlier change happened only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the service or SMTO, noting what you saw on the service. Don't repeat a change until you know whether the first one went through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Reading or decompressing the response body failed (an exception or the read deadline), or a compressed stream ended before decoder EOF, so the response is incomplete.

What this means

  • Body reading/decompression raised an exception, including a deadline, or a compressed stream ended without reaching decoder EOF. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Body reading/decompression raised an exception, including a deadline, or a compressed stream ended without reaching decoder EOF.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect complete/truncated flags and read phase without treating missing response bytes as proof a write did not occur.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the target's current state before repeating any state-changing request; for a read, reissue it with a narrower query or after fixing network stability or the request timeout on the Gateway route. Check the Gateway log for the read failure.
  • Inspect the remote resource state before repeating a state-changing request; for a read, use a fresh bounded response.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded read produces a complete response; any earlier mutation is reconciled separately.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
